candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — Health Promotion/Disease Prevention: provide education about health maintenance and recommended follow-up; assess readiness and needs related to health promotion and disease prevention
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — cancer survivorship / long-term follow-up care
candidate.educational_objective: Describe cancer survivorship follow-up as individualized ongoing care that addresses recurrence surveillance, treatment-related late effects, and physical and psychosocial health needs.

options.A: Ongoing surveillance for recurrence or new health problems, assessment of late treatment effects, and physical and emotional needs
options.B: Follow-up only if new symptoms appear, because routine post-treatment visits are unnecessary
options.C: Monitoring only for recurrence, with treatment-related and psychosocial problems managed outside survivorship care
options.D: A fixed follow-up schedule that is identical for every cancer survivor regardless of diagnosis or treatment

candidate.rationale: The National Cancer Institute states that all cancer survivors should receive follow-up care after treatment. Follow-up visits may evaluate for recurrence or other health changes, monitor problems caused by treatment including late effects, and address physical and emotional concerns. Follow-up schedules are individualized according to the cancer, treatment received, overall health, and treatment-related problems. Therefore A is the most accurate response.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Cancer survivorship follow-up is ongoing, individualized care that monitors recurrence/new health problems, treatment-related late effects, and physical and psychosocial needs.
